picks.what: The south-west prospect of Manchester and Salford, engraving
picks.why: only early general view; collegiate church (now cathedral) tower and St Ann’s spire visible

picks.what: Manchester from Kersal Moor, steel engraving after William Wyld (New York Public Library)
picks.why: classic general view of the mill town, skyline of chimneys across the Irwell

picks.what: The cathedral and Cromwell statue, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color landmark scene; cathedral tower, Cromwell statue, tram

picks.what: The city center skyline from Hartshead Pike, photograph
picks.why: whole modern skyline in one view

gaps: P0, P1: nothing. P3: nothing reliably dated (Creswick painting #3 has no date; ‘1811’ is his birth year). P5: only a vertical RAF photo and Luftwaffe target sheets, skipped.
notes: #1 is small (1009×251). #12 engraving reproduces Wyld’s 1852 watercolor for Queen Victoria; plate year unknown, so labeled 1850s. #5: Library of Congress dates the photochrom 1890, but it shows an electric trolley tram, and Manchester’s electric trams began in 1901, so labeled 1900s; maker credited as Photoglob Zürich by series convention, record names none. Many hits are other Manchesters (New Hampshire, Manchester-by-the-Sea, San Diego hotel, Providence power station), all excluded.
